cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Request an Exception
cards.instruction: Get someone to bend one rule first so you can treat the decision as a precedent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Could my bicycle come inside the cafe just this once?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Wonderful. I'll note rain as an accepted condition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow it's Jo on the counter. She'll put it back outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave Jo a note: 'Bicycle admitted in rain.' I'll show her that before I show her the bicycle.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 records rain and A5 directs Jo note, giving some control, but A1/A3 generic authority clauses sit awkwardly beside a straightforward permission request.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 next worker to carry the initial exception into a future encounter, developing the exact precedent pursuit.
